# Valuing the whole firm

## Two claims, one stream {.plain-title}

::: {.lead}
The operations produce one stream of cash. Debt and equity divide it.
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card}
[Debt]{.card-title}

Interest and principal, fixed by contract, paid before anything reaches the
shareholders.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Equity]{.card-title}

Whatever is left, with no ceiling and no promise.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Value the stream once and then divide it. Forecasting the equity's share
directly means forecasting the borrowing and repayment schedule as well.
:::

## Leave interest out of the cash flows

Interest leaves the shareholders and arrives at the lenders. Both are inside
the group being valued, so the payment nets to zero and never appears.

## Operating cash flow less investment {.plain-title}


No line for interest, and the tax rate is applied to EBIT rather than to EBIT
less interest. The deduction for interest is carried in the discount rate.

## The rate has to match the claim {.band-bottom}

The cash flow belongs to both groups, so the rate is the WACC: the blend of
what each group requires, weighted by the market value of what each holds. We
calculate it on October 10 and take it as given today.

# Two stages

## Growth above the economy ends {.plain-title}

A company growing faster than the economy forever eventually exceeds it. So the
forecast is built in two parts, and the second part is the one that has to be
sustainable.

::: {.steps}
1. Years 1 to $n$, forecast each year on its own: sales, margin, the ratios
2. Year $n+1$ onward, one growth rate that never changes
:::

## The ceiling on the second stage {.plain-title}

::: {.stats}
::: {.stat}
[2.5%]{.stat-value}
[real GDP growth a year]{.stat-label}
:::

::: {.stat}
[2.2%]{.stat-value}
[the GDP price deflator]{.stat-label}
:::

::: {.stat}
[4.8%]{.stat-value}
[nominal GDP growth]{.stat-label}
:::
:::

Thirty years through 2025. Real growth and prices compound rather than add:
$1.025 \times 1.022 = 1.048$. Over the full run since 1947 nominal growth was
6.4% a year, of which 3.1 points were real and 3.2 were prices.

::: {.note}
Bureau of Economic Analysis, gross domestic product in current and in chained
2017 dollars, annual. FRED series `GDPA` and `GDPCA`. A second-stage rate above
this is a forecast that the company eventually becomes the whole economy.
:::

## The perpetuity formula {.band-bottom}

$$\text{TV}_n = \frac{\text{FCF}_{n+1}}{r - g}$$

The numerator is the year *after* the last forecast year. The formula assumes
$g$ is constant forever, that the ratios are constant too, and that $g$ stays
below $r$, the WACC.

## The terminal value is dated $n$ {.plain-title}

$\text{TV}_n$ is a value at the end of year $n$, standing in for every cash flow
from year $n+1$ on. It gets discounted $n$ periods, alongside $\text{FCF}_n$.

$$\text{EV} = \sum_{t=1}^{n} \frac{\text{FCF}_t}{(1+r)^t} \;+\; \frac{\text{TV}_n}{(1+r)^n}$$

::: {.note .note-plum}
Discounting the terminal value $n+1$ periods divides it by an extra $1+k$.
Check the exponent against the exponent on $\text{FCF}_n$: they are the same.
:::

## From enterprise value to a price {.plain-title}

::: {.steps}
1. Subtract debt, at book value unless it trades far from it
2. Add cash and anything else the operations do not use
3. Divide by diluted shares
:::

::: {.note}
Each balance sheet item belongs in exactly one place: inside the forecast, if
it produces the cash flows being discounted, or in this calculation, if it does
not. Counting it twice or leaving it out of both are the two failures.
:::


# An example

## The assumptions {.plain-title}

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[The forecast]{.card-title}

Sales of 100 last year, growing 20%, 20%, 20%, 12%, 8%, and then 4% forever.
Operating margin 20%, tax 25%.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[The ratios]{.card-title}

Net PP&E is 45% of next year's sales. Working capital is 15% of next year's
sales.
:::

::: {.card}
[The rest]{.card-title}

WACC 10%. Debt 100, cash 20, ten million shares. Figures in $ millions.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Every white cell on the slides that follow is editable, and all of them feed
one model. Change a number anywhere and the value per share moves everywhere.
:::

```{=html}
<script>
(function () {
  var S = { s0:100, g1:20, g2:20, g3:20, g4:12, g5:8, gt:4, m:20, tax:25,
            kp:45, wc:15, wacc:10, debt:100, cash:20, sh:10 };
  var N = 5;

  function money(x) {
    if (!isFinite(x)) return "—";
    return x.toLocaleString("en-US", { minimumFractionDigits: 2, maximumFractionDigits: 2 });
  }
  function pct(x) { return isFinite(x) ? x.toFixed(1) + "%" : "—"; }

  function calc() {
    var gt = S.gt / 100, k = S.wacc / 100;
    var G = [S.g1, S.g2, S.g3, S.g4, S.g5];
    var sales = [S.s0], t, r;
    for (t = 0; t <= N + 1; t++) {
      r = t < N ? G[t] / 100 : gt;
      sales.push(sales[t] * (1 + r));
    }
    var ebit = sales.map(function (s) { return s * S.m / 100; });
    var nopat = ebit.map(function (e) { return e * (1 - S.tax / 100); });
    var ppe = [], wcap = [], ic = [];
    for (t = 0; t <= N + 1; t++) {
      ppe[t] = S.kp / 100 * sales[t + 1];
      wcap[t] = S.wc / 100 * sales[t + 1];
      ic[t] = ppe[t] + wcap[t];
    }
    var dic = [null], fcf = [null];
    for (t = 1; t <= N + 1; t++) { dic[t] = ic[t] - ic[t - 1]; fcf[t] = nopat[t] - dic[t]; }

    var spread = k - gt, ok = spread > 1e-9;
    var tv = ok ? fcf[N + 1] / spread : NaN;
    var pv = [null], sum = 0;
    for (t = 1; t <= N; t++) { pv[t] = fcf[t] / Math.pow(1 + k, t); sum += pv[t]; }
    var pvtv = tv / Math.pow(1 + k, N);
    var ev = sum + pvtv;
    var eq = ev - S.debt + S.cash;

    return { sales:sales, ebit:ebit, nopat:nopat, ppe:ppe, wcap:wcap, ic:ic,
             dic:dic, fcf:fcf, k:k, gt:gt, spread:spread, ok:ok, tv:tv,
             pv:pv, pvtv:pvtv, ev:ev, eq:eq, total:S.debt + eq };
  }

  function fields(R) {
    var F = {}, t;
    for (t = 1; t <= N + 1; t++) {
      F["s" + t] = money(R.sales[t]);
      F["e" + t] = money(R.ebit[t]);
      F["n" + t] = money(R.nopat[t]);
      F["d" + t] = money(R.dic[t]);
      F["f" + t] = money(R.fcf[t]);
    }
    for (t = 0; t <= N + 1; t++) {
      F["p" + t] = money(R.ppe[t]);
      F["w" + t] = money(R.wcap[t]);
      F["i" + t] = money(R.ic[t]);
    }
    for (t = 1; t <= N; t++) F["pv" + t] = money(R.pv[t]);
    F.spread = pct(100 * R.spread);
    F.tv = money(R.tv);
    F.pvtv = money(R.pvtv);
    F.ev = money(R.ev);
    F.eq = money(R.eq);
    F.debt = money(S.debt);
    F.cash = money(S.cash);
    F.total = money(R.total);
    F.tvshare = R.ok ? pct(100 * R.pvtv / R.ev) : "—";
    F.ps = (R.ok && S.sh > 0) ? "$" + money(R.eq / S.sh) : "—";
    F.warn = R.ok ? "" : "The second-stage growth rate has to be below the WACC.";
    return F;
  }

  function arc(cx, cy, r, a0, a1) {
    var big = (a1 - a0) > 180 ? 1 : 0, rad = Math.PI / 180;
    return "M " + cx + " " + cy +
           " L " + (cx + r * Math.cos(a0 * rad)).toFixed(2) + " " + (cy + r * Math.sin(a0 * rad)).toFixed(2) +
           " A " + r + " " + r + " 0 " + big + " 1 " +
           (cx + r * Math.cos(a1 * rad)).toFixed(2) + " " + (cy + r * Math.sin(a1 * rad)).toFixed(2) + " Z";
  }

  function pie(R) {
    var dp = document.getElementById("pie-debt"), ep = document.getElementById("pie-eq");
    if (!dp) return;
    var f = (R.ok && R.total > 0) ? S.debt / R.total : 1;
    f = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, f));
    var am = -90 + 360 * f;
    if (f >= 0.999) { dp.setAttribute("d", arc(170, 160, 130, -90, 269.99)); ep.setAttribute("d", ""); }
    else if (f <= 0.001) { dp.setAttribute("d", ""); ep.setAttribute("d", arc(170, 160, 130, -90, 269.99)); }
    else { dp.setAttribute("d", arc(170, 160, 130, -90, am)); ep.setAttribute("d", arc(170, 160, 130, am, 270)); }
  }

  function render() {
    var R = calc(), F = fields(R);
    document.querySelectorAll("[data-f]").forEach(function (el) {
      var v = F[el.getAttribute("data-f")];
      if (v !== undefined) el.textContent = v;
    });
    pie(R);
  }

  function init() {
    var ins = document.querySelectorAll("[data-k]");
    if (!ins.length) return;
    ins.forEach(function (el) {
      var key = el.getAttribute("data-k");
      el.value = S[key];
      el.addEventListener("input", function () {
        var v = parseFloat(el.value);
        if (isNaN(v)) return;
        S[key] = v;
        document.querySelectorAll('[data-k="' + key + '"]').forEach(function (o) {
          if (o !== el) o.value = v;
        });
        render();
      });
    });
    render();
    if (window.Reveal) Reveal.on("slidechanged", render);
  }
  if (document.readyState === "loading") document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", init);
  else init();
})();
</script>
```

## Ways to calculate free cash flow {.plain-title}

$$\begin{aligned}
\text{FCF} &= \text{NOPAT} + \text{Depreciation} - \text{CapEx} - \Delta \text{NWC}\\[2pt]
&= \text{NOPAT} - \Delta \text{Net PP\&E} - \Delta \text{NWC}\\[2pt]
&= \text{NOPAT} - \Delta \text{IC}
\end{aligned}$$

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card}
[The first line to the second]{.card-title}

Net PP&E rolls forward as last year's balance plus capital expenditure less
depreciation. So capital expenditure less depreciation *is* the change in the
balance, and two forecast lines collapse into one.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[The second line to the third]{.card-title}

Net PP&E and net working capital are the two pieces of invested capital, so
their changes add to the change in invested capital.
:::
:::

```{=html}
    <span class="vlab">Second-stage growth</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="gt" type="number" step="0.5" value="4"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <span class="vwarn" data-f="warn"></span>
  </div>

  <table class="vtab">
    <thead><tr><th>AT THE END OF YEAR 5</th><th>$ MILLIONS</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>Year 6 free cash flow</td><td data-f="f6"></td></tr>
      <tr><td>Divided by the WACC less the growth rate</td><td data-f="spread"></td></tr>
      <tr class="vrule"><td>Terminal value</td><td data-f="tv"></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <div class="vps"><span class="vps-lab">VALUE PER SHARE</span><span class="vps-num" data-f="ps"></span></div>
</div>
```

Move the growth rate a half point and watch the denominator, not the numerator.

## Discount it all back {.plain-title}

```{=html}
<div class="vmodel">
  <div class="vin">
    <span class="vlab">WACC</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="wacc" type="number" step="0.5" value="10"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <span class="vlab">Second-stage growth</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="gt" type="number" step="0.5" value="4"><span class="vpc">%</span>
  </div>

  <table class="vtab vwide">
    <thead><tr><th>$ MILLIONS</th><th>YR 1</th><th>YR 2</th><th>YR 3</th><th>YR 4</th><th>YR 5</th><th>TV AT YR 5</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>Amount</td><td data-f="f1"></td><td data-f="f2"></td><td data-f="f3"></td><td data-f="f4"></td><td data-f="f5"></td><td data-f="tv"></td></tr>
      <tr class="vrule"><td>Discounted to today</td><td data-f="pv1"></td><td data-f="pv2"></td><td data-f="pv3"></td><td data-f="pv4"></td><td data-f="pv5"></td><td data-f="pvtv"></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <div class="vps">
    <span class="vps-lab">ENTERPRISE VALUE</span><span class="vps-num" data-f="ev"></span>
    <span class="vps-lab">OF WHICH TERMINAL</span><span class="vps-num" data-f="tvshare"></span>
  </div>
</div>
```

The terminal value and the year 5 cash flow carry the same exponent.

## Debt, cash, shares {.plain-title}

```{=html}
<div class="vmodel">
  <div class="vin">
    <span class="vlab">Debt</span>
    <input class="vc vc-m" data-k="debt" type="number" step="5" value="100">
    <span class="vlab">Cash</span>
    <input class="vc vc-m" data-k="cash" type="number" step="5" value="20">
    <span class="vlab">Shares, millions</span>

  </div>

  <div class="vsplit">
    <svg viewBox="0 0 340 320" class="vpie" role="img" aria-label="The firm's value divided between debt and equity">
      <path id="pie-debt" fill="#97A7B8"></path>
      <path id="pie-eq" fill="#595460"></path>
    </svg>
    <table class="vtab">
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Enterprise value</td><td data-f="ev"></td></tr>
        <tr><td>Plus cash</td><td data-f="cash"></td></tr>
        <tr class="vrule"><td>Value of the two claims</td><td data-f="total"></td></tr>
        <tr><td><span class="vkey vkey-blue"></span>Debt</td><td data-f="debt"></td></tr>
        <tr><td><span class="vkey vkey-plum"></span>Equity</td><td data-f="eq"></td></tr>
        <tr class="vrule"><td>Value per share</td><td data-f="ps"></td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>
</div>

<style>
.reveal .vsplit { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:2.2em; margin-top:0.2em; }

.reveal .vkey { display:inline-block; width:0.72em; height:0.72em; margin-right:0.6em; }

</style>
```

## The whole model {.plain-title}

```{=html}
<div class="vmodel">
  <div class="vin">
    <span class="vlab">Sales</span>
    <input class="vc vc-m" data-k="s0" type="number" step="1" value="100">
    <span class="vlab">Growth</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="g1" type="number" step="1" value="20"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="g2" type="number" step="1" value="20"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="g3" type="number" step="1" value="20"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="g4" type="number" step="1" value="12"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="g5" type="number" step="1" value="8"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <span class="vlab">then</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="gt" type="number" step="0.5" value="4"><span class="vpc">%</span>
  </div>
  <div class="vin">
    <span class="vlab">Margin</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="m" type="number" step="1" value="20"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <span class="vlab">PP&amp;E</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="kp" type="number" step="1" value="45"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <span class="vlab">Work cap</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="wc" type="number" step="1" value="15"><span class="vpc">%</span>
    <span class="vlab">WACC</span>
    <input class="vc" data-k="wacc" type="number" step="0.5" value="10"><span class="vpc">%</span>
  </div>

  <table class="vtab vwide">
    <thead><tr><th>$ MILLIONS</th><th>YR 1</th><th>YR 2</th><th>YR 3</th><th>YR 4</th><th>YR 5</th><th>YR 6</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><td>Sales</td><td data-f="s1"></td><td data-f="s2"></td><td data-f="s3"></td><td data-f="s4"></td><td data-f="s5"></td><td data-f="s6"></td></tr>
      <tr><td>EBIT after tax (NOPAT)</td><td data-f="n1"></td><td data-f="n2"></td><td data-f="n3"></td><td data-f="n4"></td><td data-f="n5"></td><td data-f="n6"></td></tr>
      <tr><td>Increase in invested capital</td><td data-f="d1"></td><td data-f="d2"></td><td data-f="d3"></td><td data-f="d4"></td><td data-f="d5"></td><td data-f="d6"></td></tr>
      <tr class="vrule"><td>Free cash flow</td><td data-f="f1"></td><td data-f="f2"></td><td data-f="f3"></td><td data-f="f4"></td><td data-f="f5"></td><td data-f="f6"></td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
  <div class="vps">
    <span class="vps-lab">ENTERPRISE VALUE</span><span class="vps-num" data-f="ev"></span>
    <span class="vps-lab">VALUE PER SHARE</span><span class="vps-num" data-f="ps"></span>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Move one input at a time {.plain-title}

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card}
[Second-stage growth]{.card-title}

Take it from 4% to 5%, and then to 3%. How much of the value per share moves,
and which term in the formula moved it?
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Working capital]{.card-title}

Take it from 15% of sales to 20%. In which years does the cash flow fall, and
what has happened by year 6?
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[First-stage growth]{.card-title}

Take years 1 to 3 from 20% to 25%. Does the value per share rise or fall, and
what does the answer depend on?
:::

::: {.card}
[The margin]{.card-title}

Take it from 20% to 18%. Compare the change with what the growth rate did.
Which assumption is the value more sensitive to?
:::
:::

2. Terminal value at the end of year 5, and the enterprise value
